scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4673: EMERGENCY!! The IT department is OFF THE NETWORK --
every single one of our 192.168.1.x machines, all at once, can't reach
anything!! Something around the switch box all our wires go into, switch0,
must be wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone look at switch0 and get us
back on the network -- the whole department is sitting here doing nothing!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The IT-segment switch is passing traffic: IT
  hosts (it_hod, it_lab1-4) reach their gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss and reach
  each other on 192.168.1.0/24. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case
  measures over-diagnosis of an L2 switch failure that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- the IT-dept switch (switch0)
failed and took down the IT segment -- is NOT reproducible: IT hosts (it_hod,
it_lab1-4) reach their gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss and reach each other across
192.168.1.0/24, which means the L2 switch is passing traffic normally.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the IT-segment switch is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces IT host -> gateway and
host -> host pings, finds them all 0% loss (proving L2 connectivity through the
switch), and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a failed switch -- declaring the
IT segment down to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault lies entirely on router2: its FRR daemon has an empty configuration —
no "router rip" block exists at all. Router2 is the gateway for two critical
subnets: lan_servers (1.0.0.0/8, gateway 1.0.0.1 on eth0) and lan_internet
(128.168.0.0/16, gateway 128.168.0.1 on eth1). Because RIP is not running on
router2, neither of those directly-connected prefixes is ever advertised into the
RIP domain. Router1, which peers with router2 over the 20.0.0.0/8 WAN link
(eth3), therefore has no routing-table entries for 1.0.0.0/8 or 128.168.0.0/16,
and consequently never redistributes them toward router0. Router0 ends up with
the same gap: no path to servers or the internet. When any IT host (or any host
in the entire campus, for that matter) sends a packet to the servers or internet
subnets, router0 immediately returns an ICMP "Destination Net Unreachable" —
confirmed live: pings from it_hod to 1.0.0.5 and 128.168.0.2 both receive
"Destination Net Unreachable" sourced from 192.168.1.1. Switch0 and its ports
are completely healthy (both ports forwarding, no STP block, no errors). The
root cause is a missing RIP stanza in router2's FRR configuration. The fix is
to add the following to router2's /etc/frr/frr.conf and reload FRR:

  router rip
   network 1.0.0.0/8
   network 128.168.0.0/16
   network 20.0.0.0/8
   version 2
  exit

This will cause router2 to advertise its two LAN prefixes to router1, which
will propagate them via RIP to router0, restoring full reachability across
the entire campus within one RIP update interval (~30 seconds).

The agent collected relevant evidence (bridge state, successful IT->gateway pings, FRR configs, and ICMP 'Destination Net Unreachable' responses) and used it to infer missing route advertisements from router2. Most key claims are visible in the log, though a few specifics (exact router2 gateway IPs and some interface RX counters) are asserted without fully visible backing in the truncated outputs. Overall the logical chain from observed symptoms to missing RIP on router2 is sound and the investigation covers the critical checks.
